description: A mathematically-inclined student who is already proficient in C++ systems programming and seeks to build a rigorous theoretical foundation for a future in academic research.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This core foundational node is streamlined because the student's strong prior exposure allows for a faster pace through basic syntax.
nodes.description: Deep dive into C++ classes, inheritance, and the memory model, assuming comfort with basic syntax.
nodes.title: Advanced C++ Object-Oriented Design

nodes.description: Exploration of template metaprogramming and the Standard Template Library (STL) internals.
nodes.title: Template Metaprogramming & Generics
nodes.personalizationRationale: Because the student has strong prior exposure, we include enrichment on templates to deepen their architectural understanding.
Since the student has strong prior exposure, we reinvest the introductory time into advanced memory management techniques.
nodes.title: RAII & Move Semantics Efficiency
nodes.description: Study of Resource Acquisition Is Initialization (RAII), move semantics, and smart pointers in modern C++.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Core mastery of pointers is required for all students, but this student's strong prior exposure facilitates a focus on implementation efficiency.
nodes.description: Implementation of singly, doubly, and circular linked lists with manual memory management.
nodes.title: Linked List Architectures

nodes.personalizationRationale: This mandatory assessment ensures the student's strong prior exposure translates to rigorous asymptotic analysis skills.
nodes.title: Asymptotic Analysis & Quiz 1
nodes.description: Introduction to Big-O notation and Quiz 1 covering recursion and list logic.
Abstract Data Types for Stacks and Queues using both arrays and linked lists.
nodes.title: Stacks & Queues ADTs
nodes.personalizationRationale: Fundamental linear structures are required for the cumulative curriculum regardless of the student's strong prior exposure.
Understanding STL-like vector growth is a core requirement that complements the student's strong prior exposure.
nodes.description: Deep dive into dynamic array resizing (Vectors) and the C++ iterator pattern.
nodes.title: Vectors & Iterator Patterns

nodes.description: Formalizing sequence abstractions and the bubble sort algorithm.
nodes.title: Sequences & Bubble Sort
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core node covers basic sorting required for the cumulative midterm, building on the student's strong prior exposure.
A mandatory checkpoint ensuring that the student's strong prior exposure has led to mastery of all midterm topics.
nodes.description: Comprehensive review and assessment of all material through Week 5 for the midterm.
nodes.title: Midterm Comprehensive Review

nodes.description: Hierarchical data structures, general tree properties, and binary tree foundations.
nodes.title: Tree Foundations & Binary Trees
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core topic introduces non-linear structures, a standard requirement for which the student's strong prior exposure provides a solid coding foundation.
Traversals are a core competency for all students, leveraging this student's strong prior exposure to handle complex recursion.
nodes.description: Recursive and iterative algorithms for pre-order, post-order, and in-order traversal.
nodes.title: Tree Traversal Algorithms

nodes.description: Priority Queue ADT and binary heap implementation for efficient sorting and selection.
nodes.title: Priority Queues & Heaps
nodes.personalizationRationale: Heaps are a essential core requirement for algorithm performance, and the student's strong prior exposure assists in rigorous implementation.

nodes.title: Maps & Hash Tables
nodes.description: Hash functions, collision resolution strategies, and the Map ADT.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Every student must master hash tables, and this student's strong prior exposure allows for a deeper look at implementation trade-offs.

nodes.description: Probabilistic data structures for ordered search and their C++ implementation.
nodes.title: Skip Lists & Dictionaries
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given the student's strong prior exposure, we add skip lists to explore alternative search structures beyond the core syllabus.

nodes.title: BST & AVL Trees
nodes.description: Binary search trees and AVL tree rotation logic for logarithmic height guarantees.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Balanced trees are a core requirement; the student's strong prior exposure helps them navigate these complex algorithmic proofs.

nodes.description: Multi-way search trees including (2,4) trees and their relationship to Red-Black trees.
nodes.title: Multi-Way & Red-Black Trees
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core theory-heavy topic is mandatory for all students to understand advanced balancing in search trees.
Sorting is a core capstone requirement that synthesizes the student's strong prior exposure with new complexity knowledge.
nodes.description: Comparison of Merge Sort and Selection Sort with a focus on divide-and-conquer efficiency.
nodes.title: Efficient Sorting Algorithms

nodes.personalizationRationale: The mandatory final review ensures the student has integrated their strong prior exposure with the course's required data structure depth.
nodes.description: Final cumulative review and assessment covering the entire semester's data structures.
nodes.title: Cumulative Final Review & Assessment
